title: Soft almond turrón (Jijona style)
summary: The soft, crumbly kind of Spanish turrón: roasted almonds ground to a paste with sweetener, lemon and cinnamon, pressed into a bar.
steps: Heat the oven to 165 °C (325 °F). Roast the almonds on a tray for 10–12 minutes, until golden through. Cool.
Grind the almonds in a food processor until they pass the crumb stage and become a thick, oily paste, 3–5 minutes, scraping down often.
Warm the allulose and water in a small pan until it bubbles and reaches 115 °C (240 °F). Do not let it darken.
With the processor running, add the egg white, then pour in the hot syrup, then the zest, cinnamon and salt. Process until evenly combined.
Line a 20 x 10 cm (8 x 4 in) loaf tin with parchment, press the paste in firmly and level it. Cover and leave at room temperature for 12 hours to firm, then slice.
tips: Toast the almonds well: their roasted flavour is the whole character of turrón de Jijona.

origin.history: Turrón, an almond and honey confection, has been made around Jijona and Alicante in eastern Spain for centuries and is documented there from the sixteenth century; its roots are often traced to the sweets of Moorish Spain. Jijona gives its name to the soft, ground-almond kind, while the hard kind with whole almonds is associated with Alicante. This version replaces the honey with allulose.
